extracted.intended_audience: filmmakers and directors submitting short films to the Diogenes Tbilisi International Short Film Internet Festival
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative criteria for submitting short films to the Diogenes Tbilisi International Short Film Internet Festival (online festival focused on low-budget short films). Covers eligibility, technical requirements, content restrictions, submission materials, and selection/awards process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration of the film should be from 30 seconds up to 15.00 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival basis: “If it is impossible to project the interesting tale in 15 minutes, then there is no story or the teller is poor.” The festival aspires to select films that tell interesting stories within the 15-minute limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and application
rubrics_metrics.description: The participants should register online on the official website of the festival and fill out the application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission is fee-based (see categories & fees) and must be completed via the festival's online registration (Festhome Submission link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission materials / metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented films should be accompanied by: author(s) surname and name, author(s) 2 photos (1200 dpi each), a short biography of the author(s) (maximum 30 words), contact details, country and 3 stills from the contest film (1200 dpi each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This data will be published in the Festival Catalogue; ensure photos and stills meet the 1200 dpi requirement and bio does not exceed 30 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtitles / language accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The film should be accompanied by subtitles in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must include English subtitles so the jury/audience can evaluate films irrespective of original language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical format and orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Films participating in the competition must be presented in any digital format (including vertical format, i.e. movies shot with smartphones held vertically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical smartphone formats are explicitly accepted. Ensure file format is a common digital video format acceptable to the festival; follow upload instructions on the submission portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical clarity: image and sound
rubrics_metrics.description: The image must be visible and the voice must be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions with unreadable visuals or inaudible audio risk exclusion; maintain adequate exposure, resolution and sound levels even for low-budget productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed content types / exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The film must follow the general movie rules. TV or publicist shows will be excluded from the selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit actual short films (fiction, documentary, animation, experimental, video art, etc.). Content formatted or intended as TV episodes or publicist/media pieces is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions / prohibited subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The theme is free (no violence, no terrorism, no separatism, no religious or ethnic intolerance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While theme is otherwise free, submissions promoting violence, terrorism, separatism or intolerance on religious/ethnic grounds will be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre acceptance / engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All genres are acceptable except boring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival prioritizes interesting and polymorphous stories using simple cinematographic methods; submissions should be engaging and original. Listed categories include feature, documentary, video art/animation, experimental, horror, comedy, erotic, mobile films, youth/kids, debut, student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of submissions per author
rubrics_metrics.description: One author can present no more than two films.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors submitting multiple works must limit entries to two films total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premiere requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Films do not have to be premieres to be eligible for this festival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and evaluation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented films will be selected by a commission composed of professionals and the best works are handed over to a competent international jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival's duty is to select, objectively assess and recommend movies that use simple cinematographic methods but tell the most interesting and polymorphous stories in 15 minutes. Winners will be awarded by an international jury; one special prize/diploma by Georgian Film Academy commission; sponsors may award motivational diplomas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience award / viewer sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewer sympathy will be awarded to the film that manages to collect the highest amount of positive evaluation on Facebook and YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reception on festival social platforms (Facebook, YouTube) determines the viewer sympathy prize — encourage audience engagement and positive evaluations online.
